title: When guardians join the trade
news: Punjab's drug trade is sustained partly by a nexus of traffickers, police and politicians, exposed in the 2013 Bhola case.
syllabus: Probity in governance · Integrity and conflict of interest
link: When enforcers collude with offenders, laws lose their force and public trust collapses; integrity of the enforcer is the first line of defence.
question: As SP of a border district, you find some of your own staff protecting drug peddlers. What steps will you take, and how will you restore public trust?

title: When corruption costs power
news: A student-led movement in Serbia, sparked by a deadly canopy collapse seen as a symbol of alleged corruption, won elections and unseated the President after over a decade.
syllabus: Corruption and probity in governance · Accountability
link: Corruption erodes public trust until citizens demand accountability; a peaceful, organised movement turned that anger into political change.
question: "Unchecked corruption ultimately erodes the legitimacy of those in power." Discuss with examples.

title: When perception becomes the problem
news: Equitas Small Finance Bank's MD and CEO resigned over a 'perception issue' because his daughter co-promotes an NBFC, though he says it was disclosed and within the rules.
syllabus: Conflict of interest · Probity in governance · Integrity
link: Even a lawful, disclosed interest can look like a conflict of interest; stepping aside to protect the institution's credibility puts the institution above the self.
question: "Even a lawful and disclosed personal interest can damage public trust." Discuss the ethics of perceived conflict of interest for those who lead public institutions.

title: Who should bear the loss?
news: The Supreme Court may make banks compensate digital arrest victims where poor due diligence enabled the fraud, and noted some bank officials are involved.
syllabus: Compassion towards the weaker sections · Corruption and probity
link: Institutions that hold public money owe a duty of care: the frightened victim should not bear the loss, and insiders who collude betray public trust.
question: "Institutions, not frightened citizens, must bear the cost of systemic failures." Discuss with reference to cyber fraud.

title: Duty under fire, and money in politics
news: Punjab policemen keep manning exposed border posts despite deadly attacks, while an MP warns of gang money entering elections.
syllabus: Foundational values: dedication, fortitude · Probity in public life
link: Fortitude keeps the front line standing; probity in politics decides whether that sacrifice is undermined by crime money.
question: As SP of a border district, you learn that gangsters' relatives are contesting local elections with extortion money. What will you do?

title: When police become debt collectors
news: With civil suits taking years, influential creditors press police to turn money disputes into criminal cases.
syllabus: Probity in governance · Integrity, impartiality and non-partisanship
link: Discretion used for a powerful private party is abuse of power, even when the law is technically invoked.
question: As an SHO, an influential businessman asks you to register a cheating case against a borrower in what is clearly a civil dispute. What will you do and why?
